hints.title: Expand, then differentiate
hints.body: Multiply x1/7 through the bracket before differentiating. This gives three powers of x that you can differentiate one at a time.
hints.recap: When multiplying powers of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow></math>, add their indices.
hints.pitfall: In the derivative, multiply by the old power before reducing the power by 1.
hints.pause: Write the three terms of the derivative.

recall.reminder: When multiplying powers of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow></math>, add their indices.

hints.title: Remove the fractional powers
hints.body: Multiply your derivative by 7x6/7. This is positive on the given interval, so it does not change the sign.
hints.recap: Multiplying by a positive expression preserves its sign.
hints.pitfall: Use the given positive interval when checking the multiplier’s sign.
hints.pause: Factor the resulting quadratic and find its zeros.

recall.reminder: Factor the derivative before testing its sign.

hints.title: Mark the decreasing interval
hints.body: Put the zeros on a number line and test the signs between them. Keep only the decreasing part inside the given interval.
hints.recap: The function decreases where its derivative is negative.
hints.pitfall: Find the interval between the relevant roots; the roots themselves do not tell you its length.
hints.pause: Find that part’s length and divide by the full interval length.

recall.reminder: Factor the derivative and test its sign between its zeros to find where the function decreases.

solution:
Expanding gives f=x15/7−x8/7+x1/7, so f′=157x8/7−87x1/7+17x−6/7=17x−6/7(5x−1)(3x−1).

The prefactor is positive on (0,1). Thus f′<0 precisely when 1/5<x<1/3. This interval has length 1/3−1/5=2/15, while the full interval has length 1.

The requested fraction is 2/15: A. Including or excluding stationary endpoints would not change its length.
knowledgePattern: Factor a fractional-power derivative and measure its negative interval
